content_of_post_to_comment:
honestly, that's where my mind goes blank and i'm not thinking about anything else. no negative thoughts. not "what should i do." not "how can i make money." not "how can i clear my debts." nothing, nada.

i'm talking about boxing, which i restarted almost a month ago, and today was a good day.

my stance is getting better. my punches aren't bad. my defense is improving. my footwork still needs work.

but overall, it was a great session that i enjoyed a lot.

of course, getting hit is inevitable, but that's just how it is, and it helps a lot with becoming comfortable with fear and anxiety, which makes me a calmer person overall.

but the problem is, with the new job, it's going to be hard to attend consistently because the shifts change every week.

but i'll try to figure something out.

anyway, that's all i had for today, see you tomorrow.
comment: That feeling of having your mind go completely quiet during boxing is something a lot of people chase through meditation and never quite find. It’s interesting that getting hit, which sounds like it should add stress, is actually teaching you to stay present. Even with the shifting job, protecting that one session when you can might be worth more than chasing perfect consistency.
